ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: All directors, shareholders above 25%, and beneficial owners are screened against the Swiss SECO sanctions list (SCC), the UN Security Council consolidated sanctions list, UK and EU consolidated lists, US OFAC List and the FinCen PEP database. Screening covers politically exposed persons (domestic and foreign), their family members and close associates, and adverse media; results must be documented in the pre-corporate due diligence file and retained for a minimum of 10 years under AMLA Art. 9a. In exceptional cases with PEP identification, senior-management approval and enhanced ongoing monitoring must be implemented before signing the articles of association.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Zefix - Zentraler Firmenindex (Federal Central Company Index) and the Commercial Register Office of the Canton of Zug (Handelsregisteramt des Kantons Zug)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be stated in an authentic Swiss official language (German, French, Italian or Romansh) or be a generally comprehensible foreign expression, provided it is not misleading under Art. 950 CO. The legal form suffix must appear in the language of the articles: 'Aktiengesellschaft' or 'AG' in German, 'Société Anonyme' or 'SA' in French, 'Società Anonima' or 'SA' in Italian. The name must not contain language-confusing characters, must be transliterated into Latin script, and must avoid any word capable of suggesting an officially protected status, a non-existent larger company, or a line of business that is not objectively pursued.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the registrar issues a written negative availability certificate. The applicant may, within 10 days of receipt, file a written administrative appeal before the Commercial Register Office of the Canton of Zug; the office forwards the appeal to the Cantonal Supervisory Authority for Commercial Registers. The appeal must state the proposed exact name, grounds why the name is not misleading, evidence of registered usage or trademarks, and a request for an alternative name. Decisions of the cantonal supervisory authority may be appealed to the Federal Administrative Court (Bundesverwaltungsgericht), subject to prior notification to the Federal Commercial Register Office. If the 30-day reservation window lapses, the name is released; a re-reservation may be submitted upon payment of a new fee.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is not recognized as the statutory registered office of a Swiss Aktiengesellschaft. The company must maintain a real office address in Switzerland, normally in the canton of incorporation, where board records, accounting files, commercial correspondence and statutory registers are accessible. A professional domiciliation service provider may provide the registered address, provided it possesses material infrastructure, does not merely receive mail, and reports physical persons subject to register to the competent authorities. Use of 'virtual-only' post boxes materially increases the risk of refusing registration in Zug and may trigger a formal commercial substance assessment.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 30-35% quantified percentage for a low-risk dry-bulk sulfur trading company with non-cash settlement; the probability rises to 60-70% if the Swiss domicile provider hosts more than 25 companies or if the company appears in mid- or high-risk country trade lanes. Unannounced inspections under AMLA Art. 20 may be performed by the Financial Intelligence Unit (FIU-MROS) or the commercial registrar in connection with registration and ongoing review.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Swiss Code of Obligations (Obligationenrecht, SR 220), articles 620–659b (Aktiengesellschaft); article 637 (registration); article 643 (required charter provisions).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Handelsregisteramt (Commercial Register Office) of the canton of the registered office; for a Zug AG: Handelsregisteramt des Kantons Zug.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarized deed of incorporation (Urkunde) and certified application for commercial register entry (Anmeldung zur Handelsregistereintragung).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum nominal capital CHF 100,000. At least CHF 20,000 (20%) must be fully paid up in cash before registration. The paid-up capital must be deposited in a Swiss bank escrow/blocked account and evidenced by a banker's blocked-account confirmation (Sperrkonto-Bestätigung) which is released upon successful registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the newly incorporated Aktiengesellschaft (AG) hereby acknowledges and ratifies the full subscription and payment of the initial share capital by the founding shareholders as provided in the deed of incorporation; FURTHER RESOLVED, that the registered office is fixed at the address indicated in the articles and that all corporate books and records shall be maintained there; AND FURTHER RESOLVED, that [Name] is appointed Managing Director with sole signature authority and [Name] is appointed President of the Board of Directors, each effective immediately. All officers are instructed to make the commercial register filing and to complete statutory public filings.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarial execution of articles of incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary public of the Canton of Zug (Notariat des Kantons Zug) or another cantonal notary office.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the articles of incorporation (Statuten) satisfying OR 626. All founding shareholders, members of the board of directors, and the auditor (if required) must appear before the notary. The notary verifies the subscribed capital, the composition of the board, and the charter lawfulness. Execute and sign the public deed.
required_dossiers: Draft articles of incorporation in accordance with OR 626
Passports / ID cards of all founders and directors
Signed mandates and declarations of acceptance from directors
Note on subscribed capital and payment method (cash/non-cash)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary identifies defects in the charter or receiving signatures, correct the documents and schedule an additional notarial session; if identification documents are insufficient, provide notarized translations or certified passport copies.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening the blocked capital account and paying in minimum capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Swiss bank licensed in Switzerland; recommended: Zuger Kantonalbank or UBS AG corporate banking.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a blocked/escrow current account in the name of the company. The founders transfer at least CHF 20,000 to this account. The bank issues a formal blocked account confirmation (Sperrkonto-Bestätigung) stating the amount deposited and that the funds remain blocked until the commercial register releases them. Provide the bank with the draft charter and proof of beneficial ownership for AML/KYC.
required_dossiers: Draft articles of incorporation or certificate of confirmation
Founder and manager identification documents
AML form including beneficial owner declaration
Deposit instruction for CHF 20,000 from individual or corporate founders
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requests additional documentation (source of funds, tax residence), provide the required evidence without delay; if the transfer is delayed, obtain a payment confirmation and resubmit; no withdrawal is permitted until release by the commercial register.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing the commercial register application and achieving legal personality
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Handelsregisteramt des Kantons Zug; online via easygov.ch / SwissCommercialRegister (e-RHR).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the notarized public deed, the bank blocked-account confirmation, the signed Form 02 (New company notification), the list of board members, and the statutory declarations. Pay the registration fee. After the registry examines the file, it orders publication in the Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce (SHAB). Upon publication, the company acquires legal personality.
required_dossiers: Notarized deed of incorporation
Banker's blocked-account confirmation
Certified copy of articles of incorporation
Commercial register application form (notification of new company) with signatures
List of shareholders and beneficial owners
Power of attorney if filed by an agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registrar issues a request for correction, fulfil the omissions within the set grace period (usually 30 days). If necessary, obtain a notarial amendment. Urgent filing may be requested by paying an expedited fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Eidgenössische Steuerverwaltung (ESTV) and Kantonale Steuerverwaltung Zug.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After obtaining a commercial register extract, apply immediately for a Swiss VAT number through the ESTV portal (eVAT) if turnover may exceed CHF 100,000 or for voluntary VAT registration. Submit the cantonal tax questionnaire for corporate taxation. If the business will have employees, register for social insurance allowances (AHV) with the compensating office.
required_dossiers: Commercial register extract (Handelsregisterauszug)
Articles of incorporation
VAT registration form (online)
Cantonal tax questionnaire
Bank details and registered office address
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the VAT or tax number is not issued within SLA, follow up in writing; in case of missing information, provide corrected or supplementary declarations. Delays do not affect legal validity of the company.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate organization and registered office readiness
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registered office administration; municipal authorities of the registered address.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Set up corporate registers: share ledger, board minutes, financial books, and correspondence folders. Affix door signage if municipal regulations require. Arrange accident insurance (mandatory under UVG) for employees and workplace inspection. Ensure compliance with local fire safety and workplace safety rules.
required_dossiers: Proof of office lease/sublease
Corporate register binders and share book
Accident insurance policy confirmation (SUVA/private UVG insurer)
Fire safety attestation from the local fire inspection
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If insurance or safety certificates are missing, obtain them retroactively; if lease is insufficient, relocate or formalize sublease; municipal permit only needed for physical operations – not relevant for pure brokerage.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable – the registered business is limited to brokerage and intermediation in dry bulk marine transport of granular elemental sulfur; no physical manufacturing, warehousing or handling of sulfur takes place. For export-control purposes, SECO is the federal authority, but granular elemental sulfur is not a controlled good.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No statutory operating license required in Switzerland for the described brokerage/commodity trading activity; the company only needs its commercial register entry and social security registration.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Swiss Federal Office for the Environment (FOEN/BAFU) – not applicable for the chosen activity
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – office-based trading brokerage has no project requiring an EIA under the Swiss Environmental Impact Assessment Ordinance (EIA-V/UEIA); no construction, installation or transport operation.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: N/A – no industrial discharges or emissions from the business. Office waste must be disposed of in accordance with cantonal waste regulations; employees operate in standard office environment.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: The office premises must comply with cantonal fire-safety regulations and receive a standard fire inspection certificate if required by the building code. Occupational clearance under SUVA includes accident insurance and a workplace risk assessment; no facility-specific civil defense clearance is needed for a non-industrial brokerage office.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Swiss Federal Tax Administration (Schweizerische Eidgenössische Steuerverwaltung / Administration fédérale des contributions / Swiss Federal Tax Administration FTA-ESTV); VAT and withholding tax portal: www.estv.admin.ch; online business e-Services for VAT via Swiss Federal Tax Administration portal and Swiss Commercial Register (Zefix).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Notarially incorporate the Aktiengesellschaft (AG) and register it in the Cantonal Commercial Register of the registered office, obtaining the Swiss company identification number (Unternehmens-Identifikationsnummer, UID). Step 2: The UID, allocated by the Swiss Federal Statistical Office and shown on the commercial register extract, serves as the statutory business tax identification number for all federal tax purposes. Step 3: Register through the FTA online e-Service for VAT if annual worldwide taxable turnover exceeds the statutory threshold; foreign non-resident entities must appoint a Swiss fiscal representative and file a VAT registration application to obtain the VAT-specific number (CHE-XXX.XXX.XXX MWST). Step 4: Maintain bank account, corporate registrations and records in Swiss francs or with audited forex basis, and file through the secured FTA portal.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Switzerland does not maintain a check-the-box pass-through election for corporate entities; the AG is mandatorily subject to entity-level federal and cantonal/communal corporate income tax, with no fiscal unity or group consolidation for federal income tax purposes. Available elections affecting tax profile include: (i) voluntary Swiss VAT registration for businesses below the obligatory threshold; (ii) election to waive VAT exemption for small enterprises; (iii) option to tax real property under Article 22 of the Swiss VAT Act; and (iv) scope rules under Swiss hybrid mismatch legislation implementing BEPS Action 2, which disallow certain mismatched deductions without any elective check-the-box mechanism.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT / Mehrwertsteuer / Taxe sur la valeur ajoutée)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CHF 250,000 annual worldwide taxable turnover (excluding Swiss VAT) for mandatory registration; voluntary registration is available below this threshold and, for non-resident persons, Swiss VAT registration may be required for taxable transactions in Switzerland even without a Swiss establishment.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Switzerland does not operate a real-time fiscal clearance, continuous transaction control, or digital stamping regime for VAT invoices. There is no mandatory API-based pre-clearance of invoices with the FTA. Invoices must satisfy Swiss VAT invoice-content requirements (Article 26 of the Swiss VAT Act) and, in practice, must include supplier/recipient identification, Swiss UID/VAT number, invoice date, description of goods, quantity, consideration and VAT rate. The Swiss QR-bill is the standard machine-readable payment instrument for Swiss invoices; eBill/Peppol formats are accepted where the recipient agrees, but none constitutes a tax-authority clearance mechanism.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods exported from Switzerland to a foreign destination qualify for the 0% VAT rate under Article 23(1) of the Swiss VAT Act, provided the physical export is duly evidenced by a Swiss customs export declaration. For the bulk marine trade of granular elemental sulfur classified under ISIC 4669/NAICS 423520, zero-rating requires actual removal of goods from Swiss customs territory, commercial delivery to a non-Swiss consignee under documentary transport evidence, and retained proof that title, possession and risk passed to the foreign buyer. Directly related freight, insurance and brokerage services supplied to a foreign principal may also be zero-rated as international services where the place-of-supply rules place them outside Switzerland. The taxpayer must obtain and archive full export substantiation prior to issuing zero-rated invoices.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Swiss customs export declaration (e-dec / Ausfuhrzollanmeldung) with movement reference number, customs office release and electronic export confirmation
Commercial export invoice containing supplier and consignee identification, ISIC 4669 goods description, bulk quantity, weight, Incoterms, price and express zero-rating statement
Original through bill of lading or multimodal transport document evidencing loading of the granular sulfur and destination outside Switzerland
Bank inward remittance certificate, SWIFT MT103/MT202 credit advice, or equivalent FX receipt evidence showing payment received within the mandatory 180-day repatriation period
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Export zero-rating is subject to strict audit scrutiny by the Swiss Federal Tax Administration. If the exporter cannot produce the mandatory customs, transport and FX repatriation evidence, the FTA will retrospectively clawback the zero rate and assess Swiss VAT at 8.1% on the transaction proceeds, together with default interest and input tax adjustments. Intentional tax evasion triggers a penalty under Article 97(2) of the Swiss VAT Act of up to three times the evaded tax; negligent non-compliance attracts a penalty of up to one-third of the evaded tax. Falsifying customs declarations is separately prosecuted under the Swiss Customs Act, carrying criminal fines of up to three times the evaded duties and potential imprisonment, with a ten-year limitation period for fraud-related reclaims.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Approval of annual financial statements and the management report at the Annual General Meeting
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: General Meeting of Shareholders (not filed with a government registry)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after the balance sheet date under Swiss Code of Obligations Art. 617 ff.; court-ordered extension available only in exceptional circumstances
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: No direct government penalty for late AGM approval; persistent violations of the company-law duty may constitute grounds for a court petition to dissolve the company for serious statutory non-compliance.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual federal, cantonal and municipal corporate income tax return and net wealth tax return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cantonal Tax Administration for the company's registered seat (Federal Tax Administration receives the federal share through the cantonal collection mechanism)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Canton-dependent; for a 31 December financial year end, customary filing deadline is 31 March of the following year, with extensions to 30 September upon application
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Default interest at approximately 4.75% per annum on underpaid tax; procedural late-filing fines; administrative estimated assessment where no return is filed; intentional omissions may trigger separate tax penalty proceedings under the Swiss Federal Tax Penalty Act.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: VAT return (quarterly or annual) for taxable supplies and services
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Quarterly reporting: within 60 days after each calendar/accounting quarter; annual reporting: within 60 days after the end of the reporting period
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Default interest at 4.75% per annum; late-payment surcharge; administrative fines under Art. 179 VAT Act; in cases of tax evasion, penalty up to three times the tax evaded.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Maintenance and audit-readiness of the statutory corporate registers and share register
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Not filed with an authority; maintained at the registered office and made available to shareholders, courts, insolvency offices and tax authorities upon demand
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Ongoing obligation with no annual filing deadline; registers must be current and produced without undue delay when officially requested
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Register-keeping failures are corporate misdemeanors; directors may incur personal liability and regulatory fines; grave abandonment of statutory books may support official dissolution proceedings by the commercial register authority.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: An ordinary statutory audit is mandatorily required if, for two consecutive fiscal years, the company exceeds two of three thresholds: balance sheet total above CHF 20 million, gross sales revenue above CHF 40 million, or average annual workforce above 250 employees. Ordinary audit is also required for listed companies and for group parent companies exceeding size thresholds. A smaller AG with no more than 10 full-time equivalent employees may waive audit entirely by unanimous shareholder resolution; otherwise shareholders may appoint an audit firm for a limited review.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Swiss Code of Obligations (OR Art. 957-962) and Swiss GAAP FER constitute the statutory framework; IFRS is permitted for listed entities and consolidated financial statements. Tax accounts are prepared on the basis of the annual statutory commercial accounts.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: No general annual UBO declaration is filed with a Swiss public registry. The board of an Aktiengesellschaft must maintain an accurate share register and, for nominee structures or registered shares held by intermediaries, record the ultimate beneficial owner. Share transfers are entered into the share register upon written application; where the articles require board approval, transfer is effective only after consent. Under Swiss anti-money-laundering rules, any qualifying holding of 25% or more must be identified when the company establishes banking or commodity trading relationships.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 1,200 - USD 3,500 per annum for a Swiss registered-office/domiciliation service
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Limited review: USD 3,500 - USD 9,000; ordinary statutory audit: USD 15,000 - USD 50,000 depending on turnover and transaction complexity

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 8.5% federal corporate income tax levied on after-tax income (effective 7.83% on pre-tax profit); combined federal, cantonal and communal burden in the Canton of Zug approximately 14.6%, rising to 19.0%–21.0% in other cantons.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Participating exemption for qualifying dividends and capital gains (10% minimum shareholding or CHF 1 million threshold); patent box deduction of up to 90% of qualifying IP income; R&D super-deduction up to an additional 50% of qualifying R&D personnel costs (canton-specific caps); notional interest deduction available in selected cantons; cantonal tax holidays of up to 5–10 years for newly established companies (e.g., 5 years in Zug); special transitional relief for loss of old holding/domiciliary privileges expires on 31 December 2025.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Cantonal combined tax return 'Steuererklaerung juristische Personen' (Zug Form) filed electronically through the eTax Zug portal; the same return serves the federal direct tax (Direkte Bundessteuer) and cantonal/communal taxes, with assessment executed by the Cantonal Tax Office and federal records transferred automatically to the Swiss Federal Tax Administration (ESTV).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 6 months after the fiscal year-end (Art. 125 DBG); for a calendar-year taxpayer the deadline is 30 June; the cantonal authority grants an automatic extension to 31 August and may grant further discretionary extensions, but default interest accrues after the expiry of the legal deadline.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total gross revenue from the sale of sulfur mineral ore, freight income, brokerage commissions and incidental commercial income before deduction of expenses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report only revenue attributable to the Swiss permanent establishment (PE) or the Swiss AG itself; foreign sales routed directly through the foreign head office must be excluded and documented with a transfer pricing file.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Arm's-length cost of goods sold, ocean freight, charter hire, stevedoring, insurance, brokerage fees, administrative overhead and financing charges.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident traders must reduce the claim to expenses exclusively incurred for the Swiss PE; intercompany management fees and cost contributions must be substantiated with a contemporary TP study.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Ziffer 3 – Reingewinn (Net profit per commercial accounts)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net profit before tax as per the audited statutory financial statements of the AG, including depreciation, provisions and revaluations.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The commercial net profit must be reconciled with the Swiss statutory accounts; non-resident agreements must be adjusted for any hidden profit distributions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Ziffer 4 – Aufrechnungen (Non-deductible expenses and hidden profit distributions)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Add-back of tax-deductible free licence fees, excessive royalties, artificial rebates to foreign shareholders, and any expenditure lacking economic substance.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Any payment to a non-resident affiliate that exceeds arm's length is recharacterized as a hidden dividend distribution and subjects the Swiss company to 35% withholding tax liability.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Offset of earlier-year assessed losses against the current taxable profit; the loss pool may be carried forward for 7 years and must be applied in chronological order.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders converting a Swiss branch into an AG cannot transfer foreign losses to the Swiss entity; loss carryforward is only permitted for the Swiss taxpayer itself.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deduction of 100% of qualifying dividend income and capital gains from equity participations of at least 10% or a market value exceeding CHF 1 million.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The participation must be owned by the Swiss AG and not effectively attributed to a foreign permanent establishment; a schedule of all subsidiary holdings and bank statements must be annexed.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reduction of the taxable base of qualifying royalty/licence income from Swiss or foreign-registered patents by up to 90% (overall cap of 90% of IP-relevant income).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Trading companies without R&D nexus cannot claim the box; license-in models must pass the nexus ratio calculation documented with patent ownership chains.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final taxable profit figure after commercial-book reconciliation, deductions, participation and patent box relief; the basis for federal and cantonal tax assessment.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The final figure must be signed by the board; for non-resident controlled AGs, the tax office attaches a declaration of beneficial ownership and substance facts.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers reminder fees (CHF 100–300 per reminder), default interest of 4.5% p.a. on the resulting assessment, and procedural fines (Ordnungsbusse) up to CHF 10,000; a missing return enables the tax authority to issue a discretionary assessment with a surcharge of up to 30%; fraudulent under-declaration is penalized with a fine equal to the evaded federal tax, doubled in serious cases, plus confiscatory interest.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 35% Swiss federal withholding tax (Verrechnungssteuer) on dividends and hidden profit distributions made by the Swiss AG.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The foreign shareholder must submit a refund claim on Federal Tax Administration Form 820 within 3 years of the dividend payment date, attaching an original tax residence certificate (TRC), a beneficial ownership declaration, evidence of the shareholding percentage and holding period, and a substance attestation; after review the FTA refunds the difference between the 35% statutory rate and the applicable DTA rate, e.g., 5% under a 10% qualified corporate shareholder provision; claims are denied in cases of treaty-shopping or non-beneficial ownership.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Switzerland imposes no statutory WHT on arm's-length cross-border interest (unless the debt instrument is Swiss taxable debenture, then 35%) and no statutory WHT on royalty payments; treaty rates on interest generally range from 0% to 10% (e.g., 0% under the Swiss–US DTA), and most Swiss DTAs provide 0% withholding on royalties; a Swiss borrower must nevertheless satisfy thin-capitalization rules.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: No statutory monetary threshold exists under Swiss law; the Federal Tax Administration applies OECD TP Guidelines and requires contemporaneous documentation on request. In practice, groups with consolidated Swiss turnover above CHF 50 million or individual intercompany transactions exceeding CHF 2 million must prepare a TP study; Country-by-Country Reporting applies to groups with consolidated revenue of at least CHF 900 million.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Switzerland does not administer legacy ESR regimes, but the general anti-abuse doctrine applies: Art. 18 of the swiss Code of Obligations, the 'substance over form' principle, the OECD BEPS anti-treaty-shopping rules, and the 2020 corporate tax reform introduce mandatory substance requirements (office, staff, management, accounting, decision-making) for all Swiss AGs; a dormant or letter-box company will be denied treaty benefits, participation exemption and withholding tax refunds, and may be liquidated or re-allocated to the place of effective management.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Willful omission of taxable trading income from sulfur mineral ore sales, fabrication of cross-border purchase invoices, inflation of deductible freight and brokerage expenses, or failure to declare a Swiss permanent establishment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fine of up to 100% of the federal/cantonal tax shortfall, doubled to 200% in aggravated cases; default interest at 4.5% p.a.; discretionary assessment with a 30% surcharge; under Art. 186 of the Tax Penal Act (VStrR), tax fraud is punishable by imprisonment up to 3 years or a fine up to CHF 50,000 in addition to the tax recovery.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and signatories may be held jointly and severally liable for the unpaid corporate taxes, social security contributions and VAT, and can face criminal prosecution personally; travel bans, passport confiscation and asset freezing are routinely imposed; strict liability is imposed for false statutory accounts.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance (Art. 18 OR; 2020 Tax Reform Anti-Abuse)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the Zug AG as a brass-plate vehicle with no physical office, no employees and no management meetings in Switzerland, executing commodity resale transactions solely through foreign intermediaries to exploit Swiss treaty benefits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of participation exemption, patent box and DTA treaty relief; recharacterization of profits as taxable in the foreign effective-management jurisdiction; retroactive tax assessments and a penalty surcharge of up to 20%; removal of the company from the Commercial Register and forced liquidation under the Federal Act on Commercial Register Fees.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are personally liable for unpaid social security and tax debts under Art. 52 AHVG and Art. 12 VStrG; imprisonment up to 2 years for assisting in tax evasion; disqualification from board positions in Switzerland and potential extradition under mutual legal assistance treaties.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Withholding Tax Default and Hidden Profit Distributions (Art. 17, 39 VStG)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Making excessive payments to non-resident shareholders disguised as management fees, royalties or finance charges that are recharacterized as hidden profit distributions, while failing to withhold and remit the 35% Swiss withholding tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The AG is strictly liable for the 35% withheld tax plus default interest; wilful failure to collect or remit constitutes a criminal offence under Art. 39 VStG, punishable by a fine of up to CHF 20,000 and imprisonment up to 2 years; substantial unpaid WHT may trigger seizure of assets and a blocking order on bank accounts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are joint debtors for the WHT under Art. 17 VStG and may be personally prosecuted for non-remittance; the Swiss tax authorities issue personal penalty orders and, for large sums, pursue criminal complaints for mismanagement under Art. 165 StGB.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML and International Sanctions Violations (GwG; Art. 305bis StGB; SECO/FINMA Regime)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Handling payments for sulfur mineral ore consignments destined for embargoed territories, failing to identify the beneficial owner of a counterparty, bypassing the UBO register, or settling trades through unregulated offshore shell entities without an anti-money laundering review.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Violation of due-diligence obligations under Art. 9–13 GwG triggers administrative fines up to CHF 500,000 per case; engaging in predicate money laundering under Art. 305bis/305ter StGB is punishable by imprisonment up to 3 years and a criminal fine; SECO may freeze funds and delist the company from export licences; tax deductibility of the entire transaction is forfeited.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Individual criminal liability for directors, money-laundering reporting officers and beneficial owners, with imprisonment up to 5 years in professionally aggravated cases (Art. 305bis StGB); personal travel bans, Schengen alert issuance, book seizure and confiscation of profits are imposed; direct accessorial liability for failing to implement a valid AML compliance programme.
